newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, supported by strong packer demand for a large Saturday kill, livestock dealers said.
Slaughter Saturday was expected to be large as packers try to make up a little for lost time on Christmas, they said.
Estimates for Saturday slaughter ranged from 95,000 to 150,000 head, versus 25,000 a week ago and 221,000 last year.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog buyers said prices were steady to $0.50 higher, with country buying stations paying $52.50-$53.50 and plants $53.50-$54.50.
Illinois hog prices were up $0.50 at $51.50 to $52.00 in the country and $53.50 to $54.00 at plants.

Indiana hog prices were steady-firm, with $51.50 to $52.00 paid in the country and $53.50 to $54.00 at plants. Ohio hog prices were fully steady at $50.50 to $51.00 in the country and $52.00 to $53.00 at plants.
